page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 472 GB disk, and the server does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities but moderate to weak multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is average, while the Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 31.35 GB/sec are categorized as strong. Conversely, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core results and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth tests show a weak read-only performance of 37.14 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth remains average at 25.89 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput of 7.8 GB/sec perform at average levels.

The qualitative cost profile of the E8-4ds_v6 reflects its high memory density relative to its compute resources. The primary tradeoff is the contrast between its strong single-threaded execution and its weaker multi-core and memory read bandwidth. This hardware configuration is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling, such as medium-sized database operations, caching layers, text processing, and light web serving. It is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by the poor text generation speed of 4.5 tokens/sec on a 7B model.
